rows.explanation: Brightly coloured petals attract insects for pollination. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In an experiment to study independent inheritance of two separate traits, shape and colour of seeds, the ratio of the different combinations in the F2 progeny would be:
rows.explanation: Independent inheritance of two traits gives an F2 ratio of 9:3:3:1. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: A cross between two tall pea plants resulted in offsprings having a few dwarf plants. The gene-combination of the parental plants must be
rows.explanation: Dwarf offspring (tt) from two tall parents means both parents carried the recessive allele: Tt × Tt. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: The Phenomena of light involved in the formation of a rainbow in the sky are
rows.optionB: Refraction, dispersion and total internal reflection
rows.explanation: A rainbow forms by dispersion, refraction and internal reflection of sunlight in raindrops. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: In case of four wires of same material, the resistance will be minimum if the diameter and length of the wire respectively are
rows.explanation: R ∝ L/D². For 4D and 2L: R ∝ 2L/16D² = L/8D², the smallest of the four. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: A food chain will be more advantageous in terms of energy if it has
rows.explanation: About 90% of energy is lost at each trophic level, so a shorter food chain (fewer levels) passes on more energy. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): A piece of Zinc metal gets reddish brown coating when kept in copper sulphate solution for some time.
Reason (R): Copper is more reactive metal than Zinc.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true: zinc displaces copper. The reason is false: zinc is more reactive than copper. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Select saponification reaction from the following:
rows.explanation: Saponification is alkaline hydrolysis of an ester: CH3COOC2H5 + NaOH → CH3COONa + C2H5OH. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: United Nations Environment Programme forged an agreement to
rows.optionA: control CO2 emissions in the environment
rows.explanation: In 1987 UNEP forged an agreement to freeze CFC production at 1986 levels, to protect the ozone layer. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which one of the following statements is TRUE for Hydra, Amoeba and Spirogyra?
rows.explanation: Hydra (budding/regeneration), Amoeba (fission) and Spirogyra (fragmentation) all reproduce asexually. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Consider the following statements about ozone:
(a) Ozone is a poisonous gas.
(b) Ozone shields the earth's surface from the infrared radiation from the sun.
(c) Ozone is a product of UV radiations acting on oxygen molecule.
(d) At the lower level of the earth's atmosphere, ozone performs its most essential function.
The correct statements are:
rows.explanation: Ozone is a poisonous gas formed when UV radiation acts on O2. It shields the earth from UV (not infrared) radiation in the upper atmosphere. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Oxides of metals show basic characters.
Reason (R): Oxides of metals react with acid to form salt and water.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: metal oxides react with acids to form salt and water, which shows they are basic. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The products obtained when lead nitrate is heated in a boiling tube are:
rows.explanation: 2Pb(NO3)2 —(heat)→ 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Identify a group of the unsaturated hydrocarbons from the following:
rows.explanation: Butyne, ethene and propyne all contain double or triple bonds, so they are unsaturated. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Offsprings formed as a result of sexual reproduction produce more variations because
rows.optionA: genetic material is contributed by many parents.
rows.optionB: sexual reproduction is a lengthy process.
rows.optionC: genetic material is contributed by two individuals of same species to produce a new generation.
rows.optionD: DNA copying is not accompanied by the creation of cellular apparatus.
rows.explanation: In sexual reproduction, DNA from two parents of the same species combines, creating new combinations of variations. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Sex determination depends upon the environment in
rows.explanation: In some reptiles, the temperature at which fertilised eggs are kept determines the sex of the offspring. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Zn + 2CH3COOH → (CH3COO)2Zn + H2
The above reaction is a:
rows.explanation: Zinc displaces hydrogen from acetic acid, so it is a displacement reaction. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: An aqueous solution of a salt turns blue litmus to red. The salt could be the one obtained by the reaction of:
rows.explanation: A salt of a strong acid and a weak base (HCl + NH4OH → NH4Cl) is acidic and turns blue litmus red. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Four solutions, namely glucose, alcohol, hydrochloric acid and sulphuric acid filled in four separate beakers are connected one by one in an electric circuit with a bulb. The solutions in which the bulb will glow when current is passed are:
rows.explanation: HCl and H2SO4 ionise in water to give H⁺ ions, so they conduct. Glucose and alcohol do not. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The metals which are found in both free state as well as combined state are:
rows.explanation: Copper and silver occur both free and as compounds (sulphides or oxides). Gold and platinum occur free. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The number of single and double bonds present in a molecule of benzene (C6H6) respectively are:
rows.explanation: Kekulé benzene has 6 C–H and 3 C–C single bonds (9 single) and 3 C=C double bonds. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024, 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
In human beings, when the process of digestion is completed, the
(i) proteins, (ii) carbohydrates, and (iii) fats are respectively finally converted into:
rows.optionA: (i) Amino acids, (ii) glucose and (iii) fatty acids
rows.optionB: (i) Amino acids, (ii) glucose, (iii) fatty acids and glycerol
rows.optionC: (i) Glucose, (ii) fatty acids and glycerol, (iii) amino acids
rows.optionD: (i) Sugars, (ii) amino acids, (iii) fatty acids and glycerol
rows.explanation: Proteins → amino acids, carbohydrates → glucose, and fats → fatty acids and glycerol. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: A plant growth inhibitor hormone which causes wilting of leaves is called:
rows.explanation: Abscisic acid inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The plants that can be raised by the method of vegetative propagation are:
rows.explanation: Sugarcane, roses and grapes are commonly grown by vegetative propagation (stem cuttings or layering). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The part of seed which is a source of food during germination of seed is:
rows.explanation: Cotyledons store food used by the embryo during germination. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: A zygote is formed by the fusion of a male gamete and a female gamete. The number of chromosomes in the zygote of a human is:
rows.explanation: Gametes have 23 chromosomes each, so the zygote has 46. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The absolute refractive indices of glass and water are 3/2 and 4/3 respectively. If the speed of light in glass is 2 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed of light in water is:
rows.explanation: v_water = v_glass × (n_glass/n_water) = 2 × 10⁸ × (3/2)/(4/3) = (9/4) × 10⁸ m/s. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: When a beam of white light passes through a region having very fine dust particles, the colour of light mainly scattered in that region is:
rows.explanation: Very fine particles scatter mainly shorter wavelengths, so blue light is scattered most. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024, 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: An electric iron of resistance 20 Ω draws a current of 5 A. The heat developed in the iron in 30 seconds is:
rows.explanation: H = I²Rt = 5² × 20 × 30 = 15000 J. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Some wastes are given below :
(i) Garden waste
(ii) Ball point pen refills
(iii) Empty medicine bottles made of glass
(iv) Peels of fruits and vegetables
(v) Old cotton shirt The non-biodegradable wastes among these are:
rows.explanation: Ball-point pen refills (plastic) and glass bottles are non-biodegradable. Garden waste, peels and cotton are biodegradable. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The extraction of metals from their sulphide ores cannot take place without roasting of the ore.
Reason (R): Roasting converts sulphide ores directly into metals.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true for metals in the middle of the activity series. The reason is false: roasting converts sulphide ores into oxides, not metals. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): In the human heart ventricles have thicker muscular walls than atria.
Reason (R): Ventricles have to pump the blood into various organs.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: ventricles pump blood to the organs, so they have thicker muscular walls. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Magnetic field lines never intersect each other.
Reason (R): If they intersect, then at the point of intersection, the compass needle would point towards two directions, which is not possible.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: at an intersection the compass would point in two directions, which is impossible. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Oxygen is essential for all aerobic forms of life.
Reason (R): Free oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: aerobic organisms need oxygen for respiration. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A chemical reaction in which exchange of ions occurs between the reactants, is known as:
rows.explanation: A reaction in which ions are exchanged between reactants is a double displacement reaction. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Most of the plants close their stomata at night.
Reason (R): Closing of stomata helps to conserve water as large amount of water evaporates from the leaves.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: CO2 isn't needed for photosynthesis at night, so closing stomata conserves water. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.topic: Acids and bases in daily life
rows.questionText: The acid produced in our stomach during digestion and the base used to neutralise the excess acid during indigestion respectively are:
rows.explanation: The stomach produces HCl. Antacids such as milk of magnesia, Mg(OH)2, neutralise excess acid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The part of the flower which attracts insects for pollination is/are:
rows.explanation: Petals attract insects for pollination. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
To balance the following chemical equation, the values of the coefficients x, y and z must be respectively:
x Zn(NO3)2 → y ZnO + z NO2 + O2
rows.explanation: 2Zn(NO3)2 → 2ZnO + 4NO2 + O2, so x = 2, y = 2 and z = 4. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following is a redox reaction, but not a combination reaction?
rows.explanation: Fe2O3 + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO2 is redox (Fe2O3 reduced, CO oxidised) but not combination. The others are combination reactions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The salt present in tooth enamel is:
rows.explanation: Tooth enamel is made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite), the hardest substance in the body. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: An aqueous solution of sodium chloride is prepared in distilled water. The pH of this solution is:
rows.explanation: NaCl is a salt of a strong acid and a strong base, so its solution is neutral: pH 7. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The process in which transport of soluble products of photosynthesis takes place in plants is known as:
rows.explanation: Transport of soluble products of photosynthesis through phloem is called translocation. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The correct sequence of the path followed in a reflex action when we withdraw our hand from a hot object unconsciously is:
rows.optionA: Receptors in skin → Motor neuron → Relay neuron → Sensory neuron → Effector muscle in arm
rows.optionB: Receptors in skin → Relay neuron → Sensory neuron → Motor neuron → Effector muscle in arm
rows.optionC: Receptors in skin → Sensory neuron → Relay neuron → Motor neuron → Effector muscle in arm
rows.optionD: Receptors in skin → Sensory neuron → Effector muscle in arm → Motor neuron → Relay neuron
rows.explanation: In a reflex arc: receptor → sensory neuron → relay neuron (spinal cord) → motor neuron → effector muscle. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Sense organ in which olfactory receptors are present is:
rows.explanation: Olfactory receptors (for smell) are in the nose. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Select from the following the conditions responsible for the rapid spread of bread mould on a slice of bread :
(i) Formation of large number of spores
(ii) Presence of moisture and nutrients in bread
(iii) Low temperature
(iv) Presence of hyphae
rows.explanation: Bread mould spreads quickly because it produces many spores, and moist, nutrient-rich bread helps them grow. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: How will the image formed by a convex lens be affected, if the upper half of the lens is wrapped with a black paper?
rows.optionA: The size of the image formed will be one-half of the size of the image due to complete lens.
rows.optionB: The image of upper half of the object will not be formed.
rows.optionC: The brightness of the image will reduce.
rows.optionD: The lower half of the inverted image will not be formed.
rows.explanation: Covering half the lens lets fewer rays through. The full image still forms, but it is less bright. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: The colour of light for which the refractive index of glass is minimum, is:
rows.explanation: Red light bends least in glass because its refractive index is lowest. Violet has the highest. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The current carrying device which produces a magnetic field similar to that of a bar magnet is:
rows.explanation: A current-carrying solenoid behaves like a bar magnet, with N and S poles at its ends. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which one of the following is not a natural ecosystem?
rows.explanation: A cropland is a human-made (artificial) ecosystem. Ponds, grasslands and forests are natural. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Some vegetable oils are healthy.
Reason (R): Vegetable oils generally have long unsaturated carbon chains.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: vegetable oils with long unsaturated carbon chains are healthier than saturated animal fats. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Sex of the children will be determined by what they inherit from their mother.
Reason (R): Women have XX sex chromosomes.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: the child's sex depends on the X or Y inherited from the father. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Electrons move from lower potential to higher potential in a conductor.
Reason (R): A dry cell maintains electric potential difference across the ends of a conductor.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: electrons are negatively charged, so they move towards higher potential. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Ozone layer protects the surface of the Earth from harmful UV radiations.
Reason (R): Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) are responsible for depletion of ozone layer.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: CFCs explain the depletion, not the protection. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following is not a thermal decomposition reaction?
rows.explanation: 2AgCl → 2Ag + Cl2 takes place in sunlight (photolytic). The others need heat. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Identify an involuntary action from the following:
rows.explanation: Beating of the heart is involuntary, controlled by the medulla. The others are voluntary. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Green plants trap only 1% of the energy of sunlight that falls on their leaves.
Reason (R): All green plants are the producers in a food chain.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: green plants capture only about 1% of sunlight energy because of the limited efficiency of photosynthesis. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
In which of the following case(s) does a combination reaction occur?
I. CuO + H2
II. ZnO + C
III. Na + O2
IV. CH4 + O2
rows.explanation: Only sodium combining with oxygen (4Na + O2 → 2Na2O) forms a single product. CuO + H2 and ZnO + C are redox reactions, and CH4 + O2 is combustion giving two products. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A few drops of turmeric solution are added to a colourless liquid. If the liquid becomes red, the liquid may be:
rows.explanation: Turmeric turns red in basic solutions. Ammonium hydroxide is a base. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The acid present in nettle sting is:
rows.explanation: Nettle sting contains methanoic acid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A hydrocarbon which contains two C–C single bonds and one C≡C triple bond is:
rows.explanation: Butyne, CH≡C–CH2–CH3, has one C≡C triple bond and two C–C single bonds. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: When aqueous solutions of barium chloride and sodium sulphate react together, an insoluble substance along with aqueous solution of sodium chloride is formed. This reaction is an example of a:
rows.explanation: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 → BaSO4↓ + 2NaCl. Exchange of ions makes it a double displacement (precipitation) reaction. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: A doctor advised a person to take an injection of insulin because:
rows.optionC: he was looking short in height.
rows.optionD: his pancreas was not secreting the required hormone in proper amounts.
rows.explanation: Insulin is secreted by the pancreas and regulates blood sugar. A deficiency causes diabetes, so insulin injections are given. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The movement of sunflowers is in response to a stimulus such as:
rows.explanation: Sunflowers move in response to sunlight (day and night), a phototropic response. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In plants, waste products like resins and gums are stored in:
rows.explanation: Plants store waste products like resins and gums in old xylem. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The image formed by a concave mirror of focal length 50 cm is real and of magnification – 1. In this case the distance between the object from its own image is:
rows.explanation: A real image with m = −1 forms when the object is at C (2f = 100 cm); the image also forms at C, so the distance between them is zero. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: When we connect too many electrical appliances to a single socket in a circuit having a fixed value of current rating:
rows.optionA: the total resistance of the circuit increases.
rows.optionB: the current drawn from the source decreases.
rows.optionC: the current increases beyond the rated value.
rows.optionD: each appliance starts drawing more and more current from the source.
rows.explanation: Connecting too many appliances to one socket draws total current beyond the rated value (overloading). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Consider the following statements : I. Every step in a food chain is called a trophic level. II. Decomposers convert complex inorganic matter in dead remains of organisms into simple substances that go into the soil. III. In a food chain, energy level increases from lower trophic level to higher trophic level. IV. Linkages between various food chains constitute a food web. The correct statements is/are:
rows.explanation: Statements I and IV are true. Decomposers break complex organic (not inorganic) matter into simple substances, and energy decreases at higher trophic levels. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Biomagnification refers to the increase in the:
rows.optionC: the amount of harmful chemicals in the successive trophic levels of a food chain.
rows.optionD: number of plants and animals in an area.
rows.explanation: Biomagnification is the increase in concentration of harmful chemicals at successive trophic levels. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Soaps do not form lather (foam) with hard water.
Reason (R): Hard water has calcium and magnesium salts dissolved in it which on reacting with soap form scum.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: Ca²⁺ and Mg²⁺ salts in hard water react with soap to form insoluble scum, so lather does not form. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The commercial unit of electric energy is kilowatt hour (kWh).
Reason (R): 1 kWh = 10⁶ joule (J).
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: 1 kWh = 3.6 × 10⁶ J. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Ozone (O3) is a molecule formed by the three atoms of oxygen.
Reason (R): Ozone shields the surface of the Earth from ultraviolet (UV) radiation from the Sun.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Bleaching powder can be prepared by reacting:
rows.explanation: Bleaching powder is made by passing chlorine over dry slaked lime: Ca(OH)2 + Cl2 → CaOCl2 + H2O. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which among the following has minimum number of water of crystallisation?
rows.explanation: Gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) has 2 water molecules. Washing soda has 10, FeSO4 has 7 and CuSO4 has 5. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The opening and closing of stomatal pore depends upon:
rows.optionB: excess of CO2 in the guard cells
rows.optionC: high concentration of oxygen in the guard cells
rows.optionD: flow of water in and out of the guard cells
rows.explanation: Stomata open and close as water flows into or out of the guard cells. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which of the following statements is/are true about a neuron ? I. Dendrites of neuron pass the impulse to the axon. II. Axon of neuron carries the impulse from the cell body. III. Sensory neuron carries the impulse to the specific effectors. IV. Transmission of impulse from a neuron to a muscle fibre occurs through neuro-muscular junction.
rows.explanation: The axon carries the impulse away from the cell body, and transmission to a muscle fibre occurs at the neuromuscular junction. Dendrites pass impulses to the cell body, and sensory neurons carry impulses towards the CNS. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: A person is advised to use lenses of power – 0·25 D for the correction of his defect of vision. It implies that the person is suffering from:
rows.optionA: hypermetropia and he has to use converging lens of focal length 25 cm in his spectacles.
rows.optionB: hypermetropia and he has to use diverging lens of focal length 4 m in his spectacles.
rows.optionC: myopia and he has to use diverging lens of focal length 4 m in his spectacles.
rows.optionD: myopia and he has to use diverging lens of focal length 25 cm in his spectacles.
rows.explanation: P = −0.25 D gives f = 1/P = −4 m, a diverging lens, so the defect is myopia. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In an ecosystem, the amount of energy of sunlight captured by green plants to convert it into food energy is:
rows.explanation: Green plants convert only about 1% of the sunlight falling on their leaves into food energy. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: When lead nitrate powder is heated in a boiling tube, three substances are produced. These three substances are:
rows.explanation: 2Pb(NO3)2 → 2PbO + 4NO2 + O2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The chemical formula of Gypsum is:
rows.explanation: Gypsum is CaSO4·2H2O. Plaster of Paris is CaSO4·½H2O. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Olfactory receptors are able to detect:
rows.explanation: Olfactory receptors detect smell. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Select the correct statements regarding the cross between a pure tall pea plant and a pure short pea plant in Mendelian experiments : I. For the same trait, two copies of genes are present in individuals that reproduce sexually. II. The tall plants of F1 generation were exactly the same as the tall plants of the parent generation genetically. III. One-quarter of the plants of F2 generation were short. IV. Traits like tallness and shortness both were inherited in the plants of F1 generation.
rows.explanation: Individuals carry two copies of each gene. One quarter of the F2 plants are short. F1 plants (Tt) inherit both traits, though only tallness is expressed. F1 Tt differs genetically from the TT parent. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: When too many electrical appliances are connected to a single socket in a domestic circuit:
rows.optionA: total resistance of the circuit increases.
rows.explanation: Connecting many appliances in parallel to one socket reduces the total resistance, so the current increases (overloading). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Amongst the following groups of materials the group which contains only biodegradable materials is:
rows.explanation: Wood, leather and paper are all broken down by microorganisms, so they are biodegradable. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2024)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Electrolysis of water is a decomposition reaction. The mass ratio (MH : MO) of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes during electrolysis of water is:
rows.explanation: 2H2O → 2H2 (4 g) + O2 (32 g), so MH : MO = 1 : 8. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The products formed when Aluminium and Magnesium are burnt in the presence of air respectively are:
rows.explanation: 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3 and 2Mg + O2 → 2MgO. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Consider the following reactions :
(i) Dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide.
(ii) Magnesium oxide reacts with dilute hydrochloric acid.
(iii) Carbon dioxide reacts with sodium hydroxide. It is found that in each case:
rows.explanation: Acid + base, metal oxide + acid, and non-metal oxide + base all give salt and water. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Reaction between two elements A and B, forms a compound C. A loses electrons and B gains electrons. Which one of the following properties will not be shown by compound C?
rows.optionB: It is highly soluble in water.
rows.optionC: It has weak electrostatic forces of attraction between its oppositely charged ions.
rows.optionD: It conducts electricity in its molten state or aqueous solution.
rows.explanation: Ionic compounds have strong (not weak) electrostatic forces between ions, so they have high melting points. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The metals obtained from their molten chlorides by the process of electrolytic reduction are:
rows.explanation: Highly reactive metals like Ca, Mg, Na and K are obtained by electrolysis of their molten chlorides. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Secretion of less saliva in mouth will effect the conversion of:
rows.optionB: fats into fatty acids and glycerol
rows.explanation: Saliva contains salivary amylase, which converts starch into simple sugars. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The plant hormone whose concentration stimulates the cells to grow longer on the side of the shoot which is away from light is:
rows.explanation: Auxin diffuses to the shaded side of the shoot, where cells grow longer, so the shoot bends towards light. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
The correct/true statement(s) for a bisexual flower is/are :
(i) They possess both stamen and pistil.
(ii) They possess either stamen or pistil.
(iii) They exhibit either self-pollination or cross-pollination.
(iv) They cannot produce fruits on their own.
rows.explanation: Bisexual flowers have both stamens and pistil, and may be self- or cross-pollinated. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: If pea plants with round and green seeds (RRyy) are crossed with pea plants having wrinkled and yellow seeds (rrYY), the seeds developed by the plants of F1 generation will be:
rows.explanation: Round (R) and yellow (Y) are dominant, so F1 RrYy seeds are all round and yellow. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
The breakdown of glucose has taken the following pathway:
Glucose —(in a)→ Pyruvate + Energy —(in b)→ Lactic acid + Energy
The sites 'a' and 'b' respectively are:
rows.optionA: Mitochondria and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
rows.optionB: Cytoplasm and Oxygen rich muscle cells
rows.optionD: Cytoplasm and Oxygen deficient muscle cells
rows.explanation: Glycolysis (glucose → pyruvate) occurs in the cytoplasm. Pyruvate → lactic acid occurs in oxygen-deficient muscle cells. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Mirror ‘X’ is used to concentrate sunlight in solar furnace and Mirror ‘Y’ is fitted on the side of the vehicle to see the traffic behind the driver. Which of the following statements are true for the two mirrors ?
(i) The image formed by mirror ‘X’ is real, diminished and at its focus.
(ii) The image formed by mirror ‘Y’ is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iii) The image formed by mirror ‘X’ is virtual, diminished and erect.
(iv) The image formed by mirror ‘Y’ is real, diminished and at its focus.
rows.explanation: X (concave, solar furnace) forms a real, diminished image of the sun at its focus. Y (convex, rear-view) forms a virtual, erect, diminished image. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: An old person is suffering from an eye defect caused by weakening of ciliary muscles and diminishing flexibility of the eye lens. If the defect of vision is ‘a’ which can be corrected by lens ‘b’, then ‘a’ and ‘b’ respectively are:
rows.explanation: Weakening of the ciliary muscles and reduced lens flexibility with age is presbyopia, often corrected using bifocal lenses. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Which of the following groups do not constitute a food chain ?
(i) Wolf, rabbit, grass, lion
(ii) Plankton, man, grasshopper, fish
(iii) Hawk, grass, snake, grasshopper, frog
(iv) Grass, snake, wolf, tiger
rows.explanation: Groups (ii) and (iv) cannot be arranged as a valid producer → consumer sequence. (i) grass → rabbit → wolf → lion and (iii) grass → grasshopper → frog → snake → hawk are valid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Decomposition reactions are generally endothermic reactions.
Reason (R): Decomposition of organic matter into compost is an exothermic process.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: it is a separate exception. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): A human child bears all the basic features of human beings.
Reason (R): It looks exactly like its parents, showing very little variations.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: a child does not look exactly like its parents; sexual reproduction creates variations. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.
Reason (R): The compass needle cannot point towards two directions at the point of intersection of two magnetic field lines.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: at an intersection the compass would point in two directions, which is impossible. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in the 1980s.
Reason (R): The oxygen atoms combine with molecular oxygen to form ozone.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: the sharp drop was caused by CFCs. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: In one formula unit of salt ‘X’, seven molecules of water of crystallisation are present. The salt ‘X’ is:
rows.explanation: Ferrous sulphate crystals are FeSO4·7H2O. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: The white light entering a glass prism, gets split into its constituent colours. It is observed that:
rows.optionC: Yellow light deviates more than the blue light.
rows.optionD: Green light deviates more than the orange light.
rows.explanation: Violet deviates the most and red the least. Green (shorter wavelength) deviates more than orange. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The percentage of solar energy which is not converted into food energy by the leaves of green plants in a terrestrial ecosystem is about:
rows.explanation: Green plants convert only about 1% of solar energy into food energy, so about 99% is not converted. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Tooth enamel is made up of calcium hydroxyapatite (a crystalline form of calcium phosphate). This chemical starts corroding in the mouth when the pH is:
rows.explanation: Tooth enamel corrodes when the pH in the mouth falls below 5.5. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: The phenomenon responsible for making the smoke particles visible when a beam of sunlight enters a smoke filled room through a narrow hole is:
rows.explanation: Smoke particles become visible because they scatter light (the Tyndall effect). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The correct balanced chemical equation showing exothermic reaction in which natural gas burns in air is:
rows.explanation: CH4 + 2O2 → CO2 + 2H2O + energy is balanced and shows heat release. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The 'corrosive' warning sign must invariably be displayed on containers which contain the hydroxide of:
rows.explanation: Sodium hydroxide is a strong, corrosive alkali, so its containers carry the corrosive warning sign. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The body of human beings works within the pH range of:
rows.explanation: Our body works within a narrow pH range of about 7.0 to 7.8. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Aluminium powder is used in thermit welding because:
rows.optionA: Its reaction with iron is highly exothermic.
rows.optionB: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten iron is obtained.
rows.optionC: When it is heated with iron (III) oxide, molten aluminium oxide is obtained to join railway tracks.
rows.optionD: Its melting point is low as compared to iron and a molten alloy of iron and aluminium is formed on heating which is used to join railway tracks.
rows.explanation: Fe2O3 + 2Al → 2Fe + Al2O3 is so exothermic that iron is produced in molten form, used to join railway tracks. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Two metals zinc and tin are dissolved separately in definite proportions in molten copper (the primary metal) to obtain two different alloys respectively known as:
rows.explanation: Copper with zinc gives brass, and copper with tin gives bronze. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The opening and closing of stomata is regulated by:
rows.optionD: Amount of water in guard cells
rows.explanation: Stomata open and close as the guard cells swell or shrink with the amount of water in them. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: One-cell thick blood vessels are known as:
rows.explanation: Capillaries have walls one cell thick, allowing exchange between blood and tissues. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: When a chhui-mui (sensitive/touch-me-not) plant is touched, its leaves fold. This is due to:
rows.optionC: Change in amount of water in cells
rows.explanation: The leaves of the touch-me-not fold because cells change shape as water moves in or out, not because of growth. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Bryophyllum produces new plant through:
rows.optionA: Apical buds formed on the tip of the plant
rows.optionB: Vegetative buds produced in the notches of the leaf
rows.optionC: Flowers produced in the notches of the branches
rows.optionD: Fruits formed on the branches of the plant
rows.explanation: Bryophyllum leaves have buds in the notches of the leaf margin that grow into new plants. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The number of chromosomes in a cell division is halved. This kind of cell division is observed in:
rows.explanation: Meiosis (reduction division) occurs in germ cells of both testis and ovary to form gametes. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: If the absolute refractive indices of two media X and Y are 6/5 and 4/3 respectively, then the refractive index of Y with respect to X will be:
rows.explanation: n(Y w.r.t. X) = nY/nX = (4/3)/(6/5) = 10/9. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: An object is placed at a distance of 30 cm from the pole of a concave mirror. If its real and inverted image is formed at 60 cm in front of the mirror, the focal length of the mirror is:

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: An electric bulb is connected to a power supply of 220 V. If the current drawn by the bulb from the supply is 500 mA, the power of the bulb is:
rows.explanation: P = VI = 220 × 0.5 = 110 W. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: Four identical resistors of 12 Ω each are connected to form a square ABCD. The resistance of the network between two adjacent corners of the square is:
rows.explanation: Between adjacent corners of the square, 12 Ω is in parallel with 36 Ω: (12 × 36)/48 = 9 Ω. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The metals high up in the reactivity series cannot be obtained from their compounds by heating with carbon.
Reason (R): Displacement reactions can also be used to obtain metals.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: highly reactive metals have more affinity for oxygen than carbon, so electrolysis is used. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): A mango seed will germinate to form a mango tree.
Reason (R): Heredity determines the process by which traits and characteristics are reliably inherited from parents to offspring.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: heredity reliably passes the traits of the mango to its offspring. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Nichrome is an alloy which is commonly used in electrical heating devices such as electric irons, toasters, etc.
Reason (R): The resistivity of nichrome is high and its resistance decreases with increase in temperature.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: nichrome has high resistivity, and its resistance increases (not decreases) with temperature; it doesn't oxidise easily. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Animals will not get energy if they eat (consume) coal as food.
Reason (R): Specific enzymes are needed for the breakdown of a particular food.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: animals lack the specific enzymes to break down coal, so they cannot obtain energy from it. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A few pieces of granulated zinc are taken in a test tube and 2 mL of sodium hydroxide solution is added to it. When the contents are warmed, the product formed is:
rows.explanation: Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 (sodium zincate) + H2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The essential element used in the synthesis of proteins is:
rows.explanation: Nitrogen is an essential element for the synthesis of proteins (amino acids). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which one of the following statements is not correct for the plants raised by vegetative propagation?
rows.optionA: Can bear flowers and fruits earlier than those produced from seeds.
rows.optionB: Those plants that have lost the capacity to produce seeds can be grown.
rows.optionC: As compared to the parent plant, vegetatively propagated plants show more variations.
rows.optionD: All the plants produced in this way are genetically similar to the parent plant.
rows.explanation: Vegetatively propagated plants are genetically similar to the parent and show very little variation. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: In the human eye, most of the refraction for the light rays entering the eye occurs at the surface of:
rows.explanation: Most of the refraction of light entering the eye occurs at the outer surface of the cornea. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The resistivity of a wire made of an alloy is generally:
rows.optionA: Lower than that of its constituent metals.
rows.optionB: Higher than that of its constituent metals.
rows.optionC: Decreases with increase in its area of cross-section.
rows.optionD: Increases with increase in its length.
rows.explanation: Alloys generally have higher resistivity than their constituent metals, and resistivity doesn't depend on dimensions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Propanal and propanone are structural isomers.
Reason (R): Propanal and propanone both have the same molecular formula.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: propanal and propanone share the formula C3H6O but have different structures. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: In the electrolysis of water, the mass ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gases liberated at the electrodes is:
rows.explanation: Mass of H2 : O2 = 4 : 32 = 1 : 8. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Select the correct option from the following statements about the functioning of the human heart.
rows.optionA: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from different parts of the body and sends it to pulmonary veins.
rows.optionB: Left atrium sends oxygenated blood to right ventricle which pumps it to different parts of the body.
rows.optionC: Right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and sends it to the right ventricle.
rows.optionD: Left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the pulmonary arteries and sends it to the left ventricle.
rows.explanation: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body and passes it to the right ventricle, which pumps it to the lungs. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which of the following is the correct sequence of parts of female reproductive system of flowering plants in terms of their placement?
rows.explanation: The pistil has the stigma at top, then the style, then the ovary containing the ovules. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: The part of the human eye which can modify the curvature of the eye lens to some extent is:
rows.explanation: The ciliary muscles modify the curvature of the eye lens. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Ductility is that property of metals which enables copper to be used in making cooking utensils.
Reason (R): Copper is a metal which is ductile as well as malleable.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: copper is used for utensils because it is malleable and a good conductor of heat. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The bending of a wire in the form of a coil of several turns does not affect its electrical resistance.
Reason (R): The electrical resistance of a wire is directly proportional to its electrical resistivity.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: coiling doesn't change the wire's length, area or material, so resistance stays the same. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Consider the following chemical equation:
p Al + q H2O → r Al2O3 + s H2
To balance this chemical equation, the values of p, q, r and s must be respectively:
rows.explanation: 2Al + 3H2O → Al2O3 + 3H2, so p = 2, q = 3, r = 1, s = 3. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the given option represents a family of salts?
rows.explanation: K2SO4, Na2SO4 and CaSO4 all have the sulphate radical, so they form the family of sulphate salts. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The most common method of extraction of metals from their oxide ores is:
rows.explanation: Oxides of metals in the middle of the activity series (Zn, Fe, Pb) are most commonly reduced to the metal by heating with carbon. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Choose the incorrect statement about the common reaction used in hydrogenation of vegetable oils.
rows.optionB: It takes place in the presence of nickel or palladium catalyst.
rows.optionC: The product contains only single bonds between carbon atoms.
rows.optionD: It is an addition reaction which occurs in the presence of an acid catalyst.
rows.explanation: Hydrogenation of oils is an addition reaction catalysed by nickel or palladium, not an acid catalyst, so (d) is incorrect. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Match Column-I with Column-II and select the correct option from the choices provided.
Column-I Column-II
a. Site of fertilisation of egg with the sperm (i) Vagina
b. Site of implantation of embryo (ii) Uterus
c. Site of entry of sperm into the female reproductive (iii) Oviduct tract
d. Site through which the waste materials generated (iv) Placenta by the developing embryo are removed
(v) Cervix
rows.explanation: Fertilisation occurs in the oviduct, implantation in the uterus, sperm enter through the vagina, and embryo wastes are removed through the placenta. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The part of the brain which maintains the posture and balance of the body is:
rows.explanation: The cerebellum maintains posture and balance of the body. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The plant hormone present in greater concentration in the areas of rapidly dividing cells is:
rows.explanation: Cytokinins are present in greater concentration where cell division is rapid, such as fruits and seeds. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Select a pair of bisexual flowers from the following:
rows.explanation: Hibiscus and mustard flowers have both stamens and pistil, so they are bisexual. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The gastric glands present in the wall of the stomach release:
rows.explanation: Gastric glands release HCl, pepsin (a protein-digesting enzyme) and mucus. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The absolute refractive indices of water and glass are 4/3 and 3/2 respectively. If the speed of light in glass is 2 × 10⁸ m/s, the speed of light in water is:
rows.explanation: v_water = v_glass × (n_glass/n_water) = 2 × 10⁸ × (3/2)/(4/3) = (9/4) × 10⁸ m/s. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: A wire of length ‘l’ is gradually stretched so that its length increases to 3l. If its original resistance is R, then its new resistance will be:
rows.explanation: Stretching to 3 times the length reduces the area to 1/3 (volume constant), so R becomes 3 × 3 = 9 times. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: Which one of the following statements is not true about a bar magnet?
rows.optionA: It sets itself in north-south direction when suspended freely.
rows.optionB: It has attractive power for iron filings.
rows.optionD: The direction of magnetic field lines inside a bar magnet is from its north pole to its south pole.
rows.explanation: Inside a bar magnet the field lines run from the south pole to the north pole, so (d) is not true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): In our actions of writing or talking, our nervous system communicates with the muscles.
Reason (R): Cranial nerves and spinal nerves form the peripheral nervous system.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Magnetic field lines around a bar magnet never intersect each other.
Reason (R): Magnetic field produced by a bar magnet is a quantity that has both magnitude and direction.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: the field has a unique direction at every point, so lines cannot intersect. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Use of jute bags for shopping reduces pollution.
Reason (R): Jute is biodegradable and its bag may be reused as and when needed.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: jute bags are biodegradable and reusable, so they reduce pollution. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Study the following cases:
(i) CuSO4 + Mg →
(ii) FeSO4 + Pb →
(iii) CaSO4 + Al →
(iv) ZnSO4 + Ca →
The case/cases in which new product(s) will form is/are:
rows.explanation: Mg displaces Cu from CuSO4 and Ca displaces Zn from ZnSO4. Pb cannot displace Fe, and Al cannot displace Ca. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The part of the hind-brain controlling involuntary actions such as salivation and vomiting in humans is:
rows.explanation: The medulla in the hind-brain controls involuntary actions like salivation, vomiting and blood pressure. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Temporary finger-like extensions on the cell surface to take in food is formed in:
rows.explanation: Amoeba forms temporary finger-like extensions (pseudopodia) to engulf food. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The strength of the magnetic field produced inside a current carrying long straight solenoid does not depend upon:
rows.optionA: Area of cross-section of the tube of the solenoid
rows.optionB: Number of turns per unit length in the solenoid
rows.optionC: Direction of current flowing through the coil of the solenoid
rows.optionD: Material of the core of the solenoid
rows.explanation: The field strength depends on turns per unit length, current, cross-section and core material, but not on the direction of the current. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The growth of the pollen tubes towards ovules is an example of:
rows.explanation: Growth of pollen tubes towards ovules in response to chemicals is chemotropism. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Parasitic mode of nutrition is observed in:
rows.explanation: Cuscuta (amarbel) is a plant parasite that obtains nutrition from the host plant. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: A candle flame is placed in front of the reflecting surface of a convex mirror of focal length f. If the distance of the flame from the pole of the mirror is ‘f ’, its image is formed:
rows.optionA: at infinite distance from the mirror
rows.optionB: behind the mirror at the principal focus
rows.optionC: behind the mirror at a distance 2f
rows.optionD: behind the mirror at a distance f/2
rows.explanation: For a convex mirror (f positive) with u = −f: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 2/f, so v = f/2 behind the mirror. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: Select the correct statement from the following:
rows.optionA: The size of the molecules of air is larger than the wavelength of visible light.
rows.optionB: The blue light has a wavelength about 1.8 times greater than that of red light.
rows.optionC: When sunlight passes through the fine particles in air, they scatter the blue colour of visible light more strongly than red.
rows.optionD: The light of red colour is scattered the most by fog or smoke.
rows.explanation: Fine particles in air scatter blue light (shorter wavelength) more strongly than red, which is why the sky looks blue. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: In domestic electric circuits, the colour of insulation covers of wires in the cables of electric iron/electric toaster is generally:
rows.optionA: red for live wire, green for neutral wire and black for earth wire
rows.optionB: red for live wire, black for neutral wire and green for earth wire
rows.optionC: green for live wire, black for neutral wire and red for earth wire
rows.optionD: green for live wire, red for neutral wire and black for earth wire
rows.explanation: By convention, live wire is red, neutral is black and earth is green. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Brass is prepared by first melting copper and then dissolving tin into it in a definite proportion.
Reason (R): The primary metal of brass is copper.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: brass is copper with zinc (bronze is copper with tin). The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: In which one of the following situations a chemical reaction does not occur?
rows.optionA: Milk is left open at room temperature during summer
rows.optionC: An iron nail is left exposed to humid atmosphere
rows.explanation: Melting of glaciers is a physical change (ice to water). Souring of milk, fermentation and rusting are chemical changes. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: In order to prepare dry hydrogen chloride gas in humid atmosphere the gas produced is passed through a guard tube (drying tube) which contains:
rows.explanation: Anhydrous calcium chloride is a drying agent and absorbs moisture from the HCl gas. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The property by virtue of which a solid material can be drawn into thin wires is called:
rows.explanation: The ability to be drawn into thin wires is ductility. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Select from the following a hydrocarbon having one C–C single bond and one C≡C triple bond:
rows.explanation: Propyne, CH3–C≡CH, has one C–C single bond and one C≡C triple bond. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The essential element taken up from the soil by the plants to synthesize proteins is:
rows.explanation: Plants take nitrogen from the soil (as nitrates/nitrites) to make proteins. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Select TRUE statements about lymph from the following :
A. Lymph vessels carry lymph through the body and finally open into larger arteries.
B. Lymph contains some amount of plasma, proteins and blood cells.
C. Lymph contains some amount of plasma, proteins and red blood cells.
D. Lymph vessels carry lymph through the body and finally open into larger veins. The true statements are:
rows.explanation: Lymph contains some plasma, proteins and blood cells (but not RBCs), and lymph vessels finally open into larger veins. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Plants like rose and banana have lost the capacity to produce:
rows.explanation: Plants like rose and banana have lost the capacity to produce seeds, so they are grown vegetatively. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Ina bisexual flower the male gametes are present in the:
rows.explanation: The anther (in the stamen) produces pollen grains that contain the male gametes. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: When a pure tall pea plant is crossed with a pure dwarf pea plant, the percentage of tall pea plants in the F1 and F2 generations will be respectively:
rows.explanation: F1 are all Tt (100% tall). In F2 the ratio is 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so 75% are tall. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: To get an image of magnification —1 on a screen using a lens of focal length 20 cm, the object distance must be:
rows.explanation: Magnification −1 (real, same size) requires the object at 2F = 2 × 20 = 40 cm. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: An optical device ‘X’ is placed obliquely in the path of a narrow parallel beam of light. If the emergent beam gets displaced laterally, the device ‘X’ is:
rows.explanation: A glass slab displaces the emergent ray laterally, parallel to the incident ray. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: A piece of wire of resistance R is cut lengthwise into three identical parts. These parts are then connected in parallel. If the equivalent resistance of this combination is R', then the value of R/R' is:
rows.explanation: Each piece has R/3; three in parallel give R' = R/9, so R/R' = 9. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: An electric bulb is rated 220 V, 11 W. The resistance of its filament when it glows with a power supply of 220 V is:
rows.explanation: R = V²/P = (220)²/11 = 4400 Ω. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The minimum number of identical bulbs of rating 4 V, 6 W that can work safely with the desired brightness when connected in series with a 240 V mains supply is:
rows.explanation: Each bulb needs 4 V, so 240/4 = 60 bulbs in series share 240 V equally. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Select the most efficient food chain in terms of energy from the following:
rows.optionD: Phytoplankton → Zooplankton → Small fish → Big fish
rows.explanation: The shortest food chain, plants → man, has the least energy lost between levels, so it is the most efficient. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): In large animals, oxygen can reach different parts of the animal’s body easily.
Reason (R): Respiratory pigments take up oxygen from the air and carry it to body tissues.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: in large animals diffusion alone cannot supply oxygen to all parts. The reason is true: respiratory pigments like haemoglobin carry oxygen. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Concentrated nitric acid is diluted by adding water slowly to acid with constant stirring.
Reason (R): Concentrated nitric acid is easily soluble in water.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: concentrated acid must be added slowly to water, not water to acid, because the process is highly exothermic. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): In reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilized eggs are kept decides the sex of the offspring.
Reason (R): Sex is not genetically determined in some animals.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: in some reptiles sex is not genetically determined but depends on incubation temperature. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): When ciliary muscles contract, the eye lens becomes thin.
Reason (R): Ciliary muscles control the power of the eye lens.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: when ciliary muscles contract the lens becomes thicker (for near vision). The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which one of the following has half the number of chromosomes and half the amount of DNA as compared to the non-reproductive body cells?
rows.optionD: Both, male and female germ cells
rows.explanation: Both male and female germ cells (gametes) have half the chromosomes and DNA of body cells. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which one of the following gets biomagnified at different levels in a food chain?
rows.explanation: DDT, a non-biodegradable pesticide, gets biomagnified along food chains. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): All exothermic reactions are accompanied with evolution of heat and light.
Reason (R): Combination reactions may or may not be exothermic.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: not all exothermic reactions give out light. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: An element 'M' has 25% as many electrons in its third shell as in its second shell. The element 'M' is:
rows.explanation: The second shell has 8 electrons, and 25% of 8 is 2, so the configuration is 2, 8, 2: magnesium. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): White light is dispersed by a glass prism into seven colours.
Reason (R): The red light bends the least while the violet the most when a beam of white light passes through a glass prism.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: different colours bend by different amounts, which separates white light into its colours. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A metal M displaces iron from an aqueous solution of ferrous sulphate but fails to do so with an aqueous solution of aluminium sulphate. The metal M is:
rows.explanation: Zinc is more reactive than iron but less reactive than aluminium, so it displaces Fe but not Al. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2025)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A common feature observed in the crystals of washing soda, copper sulphate, gypsum and ferrous sulphate is that all
rows.optionC: have fixed number of molecules of water of crystallisation in one formula unit of these salts.
