rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: CO2 is far more soluble in water than O2, so it travels dissolved in plasma. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Which of the following are combination reactions?
(i) 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2
(ii) MgO + H2O → Mg(OH)2
(iii) 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3
(iv) Zn + FeSO4 → ZnSO4 + Fe
rows.explanation: MgO + H2O → Mg(OH)2 and 4Al + 3O2 → 2Al2O3 are combination reactions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A metal carbonate reacts with a solution X which forms a salt, water and a gas Y. What are X and Y?
rows.optionA: X – Sodium hydroxide, Y – Carbon dioxide
rows.optionC: X – Hydrochloric acid, Y – Carbon dioxide
rows.explanation: Metal carbonate + HCl → salt + water + CO2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: When ferrous sulphate crystals are heated in a test tube, we observe that:
rows.optionA: A colourless gas with no smell is evolved.
rows.optionC: The green colour of the salt fades and a gas with the smell of burning sulphur is evolved.
rows.optionD: The green colour of the salt fades and no gas is evolved.
rows.explanation: On heating, green FeSO4 crystals lose water and decompose, giving SO2 and SO3 with the smell of burning sulphur. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: When Mg metal is treated with hot water, it starts floating on the surface of the water. The reason for its different behaviour is:
rows.optionA: Mg is a lighter element than water.
rows.optionB: Mg reacts with water to produce H2 gas which helps in floating.
rows.optionC: Mg reacts with water to produce N2 gas which helps in floating.
rows.optionD: Mg reacts with water to form CO2 gas which helps in floating.
rows.explanation: Magnesium reacts with hot water to form H2 bubbles, which stick to its surface and make it float. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The pH of the gastric juices released during digestion is:
rows.explanation: Gastric juice contains HCl, so its pH is less than 7 (strongly acidic). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Baking powder is a mixture of:
rows.explanation: Baking powder is a mixture of baking soda (NaHCO3) and a mild edible acid such as tartaric acid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Carbon compounds can form chains, branched and ring structures.
Reason (R): Carbon exhibits the property of catenation.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: catenation lets carbon atoms link into chains, branches and rings. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: From the following options choose the one which gives negative magnification greater than one:
rows.optionA: Concave mirror; Nature of image – real
rows.optionB: Concave mirror; Nature of image – virtual
rows.optionC: Convex mirror; Nature of image – real
rows.optionD: Convex mirror; Nature of image – virtual
rows.explanation: A negative magnification greater than one (real, inverted, enlarged image) is produced only by a concave mirror with the object between F and C. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Direction of force exerted on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field remains the same if the directions of both magnetic field and current flowing through the conductor are reversed.
Reason (R): The direction of force exerted on a current-carrying conductor placed in an external magnetic field can be determined by using a magnetic compass.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: the direction of force is found by Fleming's left-hand rule, not by a compass. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: If the stomatal pore is open, it indicates which situation from the following?
rows.optionB: The water comes out of the guard cells.
rows.optionC: Large amount of water is lost through stomata.
rows.optionD: The guard cells have swelled due to inflow of water.
rows.explanation: Stomata open when guard cells swell due to inflow of water. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which of the following limits the number of trophic levels in a food chain?
rows.optionC: Decrease in energy at higher levels
rows.explanation: Energy decreases at each higher trophic level (only 10% passes on), which limits food chains to 3–4 levels. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Tamarind is a natural source of which acid?
rows.explanation: Tamarind contains tartaric acid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Rain water is called ‘acid rain’ when its:
rows.explanation: Rain water with pH below 5.6 is called acid rain. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: A student notices that her silver jewellery turned dull and had a grey-black coating over it after wearing for a few months. What results in the change in colour of the silver metal?
rows.optionA: The polish over the jewellery was removed after wearing for a few months.
rows.optionB: The jewellery comes in contact with air, moisture and acids and corrodes.
rows.optionC: Dust particles over the jewellery change its colour.
rows.optionD: Its colour changes due to rusting.
rows.explanation: Silver reacts with sulphur compounds in air to form a black coating of silver sulphide (tarnishing), a form of corrosion. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Carbon shows the property of catenation.
Reason (R): C – C bond is weak due to its small size.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: the C–C bond is very strong because of carbon's small size. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText: A thin beam of white light falls on a face of a glass prism and a spectrum is obtained on a screen. Which of the following options is the correct sequence of colours from top to bottom on the screen?
rows.explanation: Red deviates least and violet most, so on the screen the order from top to bottom is red, yellow, green, blue, violet. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Select the option that represents the correct balanced equation for the process of photosynthesis : Chlorophyll
rows.optionA: CO2 + O2 + H2O —(chlorophyll, sunlight)→ C6H12O6 + H2O
rows.explanation: The balanced equation is 6CO2 + 12H2O → C6H12O6 + 6O2 + 6H2O, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following compounds is used for removing permanent hardness of water?
rows.explanation: Washing soda removes permanent hardness of water. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Which of the following are decomposition reactions?
(i) 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2
(ii) MgO + H2O → Mg(OH)2
(iii) 2H2O → 2H2 + O2
(iv) Zn + CuSO4 → ZnSO4 + Cu
rows.explanation: 2KClO3 → 2KCl + 3O2 and 2H2O → 2H2 + O2 are decomposition reactions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Pravin was given a list of characteristics of anaerobic respiration in humans:
(i) Location – Muscle cell
(ii) Condition – Requires presence of oxygen (O2) and carbon dioxide (CO2)
(iii) End product – 3-carbon molecules
Which of these characteristics is/are related to the process?
rows.explanation: Anaerobic respiration in humans occurs in muscle cells without oxygen, and its end product is lactic acid, a 3-carbon molecule. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In an activity to show that CO2 is necessary for photosynthesis, two potted plants are used; one jar contains a watch-glass with potassium hydroxide. Identify the incorrect step in the set-up:
rows.optionA: Both plants are kept in the dark room for three days before placing them in separate glass jars.
rows.optionB: Both plants are covered with separate wooden bell-jars.
rows.optionC: Use vaseline to seal the bottom of the jars with the glass plates.
rows.optionD: Both potted plants were kept in sunlight for a few hours before the iodine test for the presence of starch.
rows.explanation: Plants must be covered with transparent glass bell-jars so light can reach them. Wooden bell-jars would block light, so (b) is the incorrect step. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Walking in a straight line and riding a bicycle are activities possible due to coordination by which part of the brain? (Part of the brain — Name of the area)
rows.explanation: The cerebellum, in the hind-brain, coordinates balance and precise movements like walking and cycling. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In a synapse, the chemical signal is transmitted from:
rows.optionA: Dendritic end of one neuron to axonal end of another neuron.
rows.optionB: Axon to cell body of the same neuron.
rows.optionC: Cell body to axonal end of the same neuron.
rows.optionD: Axonal end of one neuron to dendritic end of another neuron.
rows.explanation: At a synapse, chemicals released from the axonal end of one neuron cross to the dendritic end of the next. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Organisms of a higher trophic level which feed on several types of organisms belonging to a lower trophic level form the:
rows.explanation: When organisms feed on several types of lower-level organisms, the interconnected food chains form a food web. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: In accumulation of toxic substances at higher trophic levels of an ecosystem through the food chain, which of the following organisms is affected the most?
rows.explanation: Humans occupy the top trophic level in many food chains, so they accumulate the most toxic chemicals. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Natural replenishment of soil will not take place in absence of microbes.
Reason (R): Microbes, comprising of bacteria and fungi, break down dead remains and waste products of organisms, and they go into the soil.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: decomposers break down dead remains and return nutrients to the soil. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): The basic filtration unit in the kidneys, like in the lungs, is a cluster of very thin-walled blood capillaries.
Reason (R): Each capillary cluster in the kidney is associated with the cup-shaped end of a coiled tube called Bowman’s capsule.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion: it only describes the structure of the nephron. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following is an example of a displacement reaction?
rows.optionB: The reaction of a reactive metal with dilute acid
rows.optionD: The reaction of quick lime with water
rows.explanation: A reactive metal displaces hydrogen from a dilute acid, so it is a displacement reaction. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.topic: Reaction of metal oxides with acids
rows.questionText: To a small amount of copper oxide in a beaker, when we add dilute hydrochloric acid slowly with stirring, the change in the colour of the solution is due to the formation of:
rows.optionA: Copper(II) oxide, which is black in colour.
rows.optionB: Copper(I) chloride, which is blue in colour.
rows.optionC: Copper(II) chloride, which is blue-green in colour.
rows.optionD: Copper(I) oxide, which is black in colour.
rows.explanation: CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O. Copper(II) chloride gives the solution a blue-green colour. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
In the following equation:
x KI + H2O2 → I2 + y KOH
x and y respectively are:
rows.explanation: 2KI + H2O2 → I2 + 2KOH, so x = 2 and y = 2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Consider the structures 'X' = CH3–CH2–CH2–CH3 and 'Y' = CH3–CH(CH3)–CH3.
Which of the following statements are correct?
(i) 'X' and 'Y' are homologues.
(ii) 'X' and 'Y' have the same structural formula, but different molecular formula.
(iii) 'X' and 'Y' have the same molecular formula, but different structural formula.
(iv) 'X' and 'Y' are structural isomers.
rows.explanation: X (n-butane) and Y (isobutane) share the formula C4H10 but have different structures, so they are structural isomers. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The reaction of calcium with cold water is:
rows.optionA: Less violent, but the heat evolved is sufficient for the hydrogen to catch fire.
rows.optionB: Very violent and exothermic and hydrogen catches fire.
rows.optionC: Exothermic, but the heat evolved is not sufficient for the hydrogen to catch fire.
rows.explanation: Calcium reacts less violently with cold water; the heat is not enough for the hydrogen to catch fire, and calcium floats on the H2 bubbles. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): There are large number of compounds with many carbon atoms linked to each other.
Reason (R): Carbon-Carbon bond is very strong and stable.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: the strong, stable C–C bond allows long carbon chains, giving a huge number of compounds. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: The correct way to connect an ammeter and a voltmeter in an electric circuit is:
rows.optionA: Ammeter in parallel and voltmeter in series
rows.optionB: Ammeter and voltmeter both in parallel
rows.optionC: Ammeter in series and voltmeter in parallel
rows.optionD: Ammeter and voltmeter both in series
rows.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series and a voltmeter in parallel. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: The growth of tendrils in grapes plants is due to:
rows.optionC: Rapid cell division in tendril cells in contact with the support
rows.optionD: Rapid cell division in tendril cells that are away from the support
rows.explanation: Cells of the tendril away from the support divide and grow faster, making the tendril coil around the support. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Ozone (O3) gas at higher levels of atmosphere is a product of UV radiation acting on Oxygen (O2).
Reason (R): The amount of ozone in the atmosphere began to drop sharply in 1980s.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true, but the reason does not explain the assertion. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: When zinc reacts with NaOH, the product formed is:
rows.explanation: Zn + 2NaOH → Na2ZnO2 (sodium zincate) + H2. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: In an electric circuit carrying current I, a 2 Ω resistor is replaced by an 8 Ω resistor without changing the connected (ideal) battery. Then:
rows.optionA: current becomes I/4 and potential difference becomes V/4
rows.optionB: current becomes I/4 and potential difference remains V
rows.optionC: current becomes 4I and potential difference remains V
rows.optionD: current becomes 4I and potential difference becomes V/4
rows.explanation: With the same ideal battery, V stays the same. Resistance becomes 4 times, so the current becomes I/4. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which of the following represents the correct sequence of events of sexual reproduction in a flower?
rows.explanation: The sequence is pollination → fertilisation → embryo → seed. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Arteries have valves as they have to withstand high pressure.
Reason (R): Arteries are vessels which carry blood away from the heart to various organs.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is false: arteries have thick elastic walls, and valves are found in veins. The reason is true. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following compounds does not undergo addition reaction?
rows.explanation: C3H8 (propane) is saturated, so it does not undergo addition reactions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which structure in a leaf is mainly responsible for gaseous exchange?
rows.explanation: Stomata are the main sites of gaseous exchange in leaves. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Identify the correct statement for spirogyra, leishmania and hydra:
rows.explanation: Spirogyra (fragmentation), Leishmania (binary fission) and Hydra (budding/regeneration) all reproduce asexually. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Human brain has various parts or regions that help in different actions, responses and coordination. From the following, identify the part responsible for precision of voluntary actions:
rows.explanation: The cerebellum is responsible for the precision of voluntary actions, posture and balance. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Pancreas secretes pancreatic juice which contain certain enzyme that helps in digestion of food.
Choose the correct option from the following:
rows.optionA: Trypsin digests emulsified fats and lipase digests proteins.
rows.optionB: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests emulsified fats.
rows.optionC: Trypsin and lipase both digests fats.
rows.optionD: Trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests carbohydrates.
rows.explanation: In pancreatic juice, trypsin digests proteins and lipase digests emulsified fats. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText: Which of the following group is not ‘biodegradable’?
rows.optionC: Polythene bag, rubber band, ball pen
rows.explanation: Polythene bags, rubber bands and ball pens are non-biodegradable. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Reflex actions do not involve thinking.
Reason (R): Most reflex actions are controlled by the spinal cord.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: reflexes are controlled by the spinal cord, so no thinking by the brain is involved. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Biology
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): In human beings, the respiratory pigment is haemoglobin present in red blood cells.
Reason (R): Haemoglobin has a very high affinity for carbon dioxide.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: haemoglobin has a very high affinity for oxygen, not carbon dioxide. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
(i) AgNO3 + NaCl → NaNO3 + AgCl
(ii) K2SO4 + BaCl2 → BaSO4 + 2KCl
Which of the following options correctly describes both reactions?
rows.optionA: (i) is double displacement, (ii) is displacement reaction.
rows.optionB: Both, (i) and (ii) are displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
rows.optionC: Both, (i) and (ii) are double displacement reactions and precipitation reactions.
rows.optionD: (i) is displacement, (ii) is double displacement reaction.
rows.explanation: Both reactions exchange ions and form insoluble precipitates (AgCl, BaSO4), so they are double displacement and precipitation reactions. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which one of the following can be used as an acid-base indicator by a visually impaired (blind) student?
rows.explanation: Vanilla essence is an olfactory indicator: its smell changes with acids and bases. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The gases evolved on heating lead (II) nitrate crystals are:
rows.explanation: Lead nitrate decomposes to give NO2 and O2 (with PbO left behind). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The formula of functional group for aldehyde is:
rows.explanation: The aldehyde functional group is –CHO. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: Which of the following is a poor conductor of electricity?
rows.explanation: Lead is a comparatively poor conductor of electricity. Cu, Ag and Al are good conductors. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText: The natural sources of oxalic acid, lactic acid and methanoic acid respectively are:
rows.explanation: Tomato contains oxalic acid, curd lactic acid and ant sting methanoic acid. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Chemistry
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): Carbon shares its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements.
Reason (R): The shared electrons belong to the outermost shells of both the atoms and lead to both atoms attaining the noble gas configuration.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: carbon shares electrons so both atoms reach a noble gas configuration. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.questionText: A convex lens of focal length 15 cm, is forming a real image. If the size of image is same as the size of object, then position of object and position of image will be, respectively:
rows.explanation: A same-size real image forms with the object at 2F (−30 cm); the image forms at 2F on the other side (+30 cm). (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.subject: Physics
rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.questionText:
Assertion (A): When rays of white light pass through a prism, on emerging they give spectrum of seven colours.
Reason (R): It is due to the scattering of light that red light bends minimum and violet light bends the maximum.
rows.optionA: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionB: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
rows.optionC: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
rows.optionD: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
rows.explanation: The assertion is true. The reason is false: different colours bend by different amounts because of dispersion, not scattering. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)

rows.questionText: When you look at an object very close to your eyes, the:
rows.optionA: Ciliary muscles of your eye contract and the eye lens becomes thick.
rows.optionB: Ciliary muscles of your eye get relaxed and the eye lens becomes thick.
rows.optionC: Ciliary muscles of your eye contract and the eye lens becomes thin.
rows.optionD: Ciliary muscles of your eye get relaxed and the eye lens becomes thin.
rows.explanation: For near objects the ciliary muscles contract, making the lens thicker to shorten its focal length. (CBSE Class 10 Science 2026)
